task.title: Configuring programmatic bootstrap on standalone deployments
task.shortdesc: To configure filesystem-based bootstrap OAuth token provisioning in a standalone Red Hat Quay deployment, you can set FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP and related fields in the config.yaml file, then restart the registry.

ul.li: You have a standalone Red Hat Quay deployment with at least one superuser account created.
You can modify the Red Hat Quay config.yaml file.

step.cmd: Set the following fields in your Red Hat Quay config.yaml file:

info.codeblock: FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP: true SUPER_USERS: - quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_OWNER: quayadmin BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_EXPIRATION: 7776000 BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SCOPE: "org:admin repo:admin repo:create repo:read repo:write super:user user:admin user:read" BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH: /datastorage/bootstrap-token.json
info.p: Set BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_PATH to a directory that the Red Hat Quay process can write. In containerized standalone deployments, use a mounted storage path such as /datastorage/bootstrap-token.json. Quote the BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_SCOPE value so YAML does not misparse scopes that contain :.

step.cmd: Restart Red Hat Quay after you update the configuration.

note.p: If you enable FEATURE_PROGRAMMATIC_BOOTSTRAP on a deployment that is already running, you must restart Red Hat Quay so the bootstrap token is provisioned and the POST /api/v1/bootstrap/renew endpoint is registered. A full restart is required; reloading configuration without restarting does not register the bootstrap API endpoints.

substep.cmd: Check Red Hat Quay startup logs for a Bootstrap token provisioned message.
